# Intake Draft — Add parent field to concise format of wl show output (WL-0MW5M5GUF0051D4N)

## Problem statement

The concise format of `wl show` (`-F concise`) omits the parent relationship entirely: an item with a parent shows no indication of it, so a user must switch to `normal` or `full` format to see which parent item a work item belongs to. The `normal` and `full` formats both already render a conditional `Parent` row; the `concise` format should do the same.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using `wl show -F concise` (and `wl list -F concise`, which reuses the same formatter) to inspect work items compactly.
  - User story: As a user viewing a work item in concise format, I want to see its parent ID so I can trace the item's position in the work hierarchy without switching format.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl show <id> -F concise` renders a `Parent` row in the metadata table when the item has a `parentId` set, displaying the parent's ID. The row sits after `Effort` and before `Assignee`, matching the `normal`/`full` row order.
2. When the item has no parent, no `Parent` row appears in concise output (the row is conditional on `parentId` being set).
3. The `Parent` row renders correctly in both plain-text and markdown/TTY rendering of the concise format.
4. `wl list -F concise` tree rendering reflects the same change without regressing tree output (it delegates to the same formatter).
5. A unit test asserts the `Parent` row appears in concise output when `parentId` is set and is absent when it is not; all existing tests pass with the change.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Users of `wl show -F concise` can now see an item's parent at a glance, instead of switching to normal/full output to trace the hierarchy.

## Constraints

- **No changes** to `summary`, `raw`, `--fields` projected output, `normal`, or `full` formats.
- The `Parent` row is conditional on `parentId` being truthy — never a placeholder row in concise mode.
- Preserve the existing concise row order; insert `Parent` after `Effort`, before `Assignee`, consistent with `normal`/`full`.

## Existing state

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` → `humanFormatWorkItem()`: both `full` and `normal` format blocks already include `if (item.parentId) metaRows.push(['Parent', item.parentId]);`.
- The `concise` block (in the same function) builds its metadata table with: `Status` (incl. Stage | Priority), `SortIndex`, `Risk`, `Effort`, then conditional `Assignee`, `Audit`, `Tags` — no `Parent` row.
- Concise format is used by `wl show -F concise` and reused by the tree renderer `displayItemTreeWithFormat(items, db, 'concise')` for `wl list -F concise`.

## Desired change

- Add `if (item.parentId) metaRows.push(['Parent', item.parentId]);` to the `concise` block of `humanFormatWorkItem()` in `src/commands/helpers.ts`, after the `Effort` row.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — Add the conditional `Parent` row to the concise block of `humanFormatWorkItem()`.
- `tests/cli/helpers-tree-rendering.test.ts` — Logically adjacent concise-format tests (Risk/Effort rows); candidate home for the new coverage.
- `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` — Snapshot tests of concise/normal/full; items have no `parentId`, so unaffected, but adjacent precedent.
- `tests/integration/wl-show-formatting.test.ts` — Formatting integration tests (mock item has `parentId: null`; unaffected).
- `CLI.md` — `-F concise` documented only by examples; verify no row-by-row description needs updating.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: the `if (item.parentId)` truthiness guard matches `normal`/`full` behaviour (an empty string is treated as "no parent").
- **Assumption**: snapshot tests in `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` and `tests/cli/human-show-list-audit-snapshots.test.ts` use items without a parent, so no snapshot churn is expected; verify on run.
- **Scope-creep guard**: `--fields` projected output and `-f summary` are explicitly out of scope (recorded in Constraints); if the producer later wants them, they should be linked work items, not scope creep here.
- **Risk (low)**: `wl list -F concise` tree output will now include a `Parent` row per item — intended, but tree-rendering tests should be checked (AC4).

## Related work

- `WL-0MS6MOXNQ005B9IC` — Metadata in work-item detail views should be presented as markdown table (completed): established the markdown metadata table in full/normal/concise and the `Parent` row in full/normal; this item closes the concise-format gap.
- `WL-0MP14VZP8008ETDV` — Add integration tests for wl show formatted vs plain output (TTY/non-TTY) (completed): test precedent for show formatting.
- `WL-0MP14VZZG009KHPR` — Docs: document --format flag and CLI markdown behaviour (completed): `-F`/format documentation precedent.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **WL-0MMNCOJ0V0IFM2SN** – Audit Read Path in Show Outputs (completed)
- **WL-0MM8LXZ0M04W2YUF** – Human-readable and JSON output formatting (completed)
- **WL-0MS6MOXNQ005B9IC** – Metadata in work-item detail views should be presented as markdown table (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `CLI.md` — matched: add, concise, field, format, output (+2 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, field, format, output, parent (+1 more)
- `DATA_SYNCING.md` — matched: add, field, format, output, parent (+1 more)


## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "When should the `Parent` row appear in `-F concise` output — (a) only when `parentId` is set (conditional, matching normal/full), or (b) always with a `—` placeholder like Risk/Effort?" — Answer (operator): "(a) — conditional". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope — (a) only the `-F concise` human format, or (b) also `--fields` projected output and/or `-F summary`?" — Answer (operator): "(a) — `-F concise` only". Source: interactive reply.

# Ship opens in own tab (WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU)

**Headline**: The Ship It shortcut (`S`) dispatches the dev→main release (`/skill:ship release`) into a pi pane that currently splits the **current tab**. Change it so the release runs in **its own tab labelled `Ship`** in the invoking workspace — created on first use, reused thereafter, focused on open, placed left of the extensions/Work Items tab — and reject a second Ship command while the first release is still active.

## Problem statement

When an operator presses `S` in the herdr worklist selection list and confirms with `ship` + Enter, the release pi pane opens by splitting the current pane/tab, scattering the release in whatever tab the operator happened to be in. Ship is already a distinct, guarded workflow (typed-confirmation dialog, ship guard, code-freeze marker), so its pane should live in a dedicated, recognisable `Ship` tab — and a second release must not be started while the first is still running.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running a dev→main release**:
  > "As an operator, when I press `S` and confirm `ship`, I want the release pi session to open in a tab titled **Ship** so I can find it immediately and keep the release runner separate from the selection list and other work-tabs."
- **Operator running repeated releases**:
  > "As an operator who ships several times a day, I want the Ship tab to be reused (one release per tab) and a second Ship command rejected while a release is still active, so I never accidentally start two releases or clutter the tab row."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ship dispatch opens in its own tab** — pressing `S` and confirming with `ship` + Enter dispatches `/skill:ship release` into a tab labelled exactly `Ship` in the invoking pane's current workspace (created on first use, reused thereafter) instead of splitting the current pane/tab. Verified via `herdr tab list --workspace <ws>` (`label == 'Ship'`) and the spawned pi pane's `tab_id` matching that tab.
2. **Second Ship while active is rejected** — while the first release is still active (its Ship pane is live), a second `S` → confirm does **not** dispatch: a blocked notice is shown (no dialog/confirm opens), mirroring the existing ship-guard behaviour. No second pi pane is spawned.
3. **Focus the Ship pane** — the release pi pane is focused/zoomed on open so the operator immediately sees the release run (the pane may still be focused without stealing list focus, consistent with `focus: true` shortcut behaviour).
4. **Fresh Ship tab placed left-of-extensions** — a newly created `Ship` tab is placed immediately left of the extensions/Work Items tab (`'left-of-extensions'`), matching interactive item-ID tab placement; a reused tab is never repositioned.
5. **Fail-open placement** — if the `Ship` tab cannot be resolved or created (CLI failure, no workspace, guard query failure), the dispatch falls back to the current-pane split exactly as today — the release is never blocked by tab provisioning.
6. **Testing/validation** — unit + TUI integration tests cover: the Ship pane lands in the `Ship` tab (anchor pane id forwarded to `send-to-pi.sh`); the rejected second-command path; focus forwarding; left-of-extensions placement of a fresh tab; and the fail-open fallback.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs-site or wiki entries (e.g. the ship-it dialog / placement docs).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators can now start a dev→main release from the worklist and watch it run in a dedicated, always-findable `Ship` tab — with a fresh tab placed beside the work items and a second release safely rejected while the first is still running.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing interactive tab machinery (`getItemTabAnchor` / `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <label> --no-focus`) — do not introduce a parallel tab-provisioning path.
- The typed ship confirmation dialog (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY), ship guard (WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW) and code-freeze marker flow stay intact; this item changes only *where* the dispatch pane lands and adds the second-command rejection.
- Global release command: `/skill:ship release` carries **no work-item ID**, so today `interactiveItemId` is `undefined` and the interactive item-ID anchor path returns `null`. The `Ship` label must be substituted for the missing item ID on this path only.
- Focus is currently *not* passed for the ship dispatch (`--no-focus`); this item adds focus explicitly.
- No push to `main`; work is committed to `dev` per the push policy.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `S` → `/skill:ship release` (view `both`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `openShipItDialogGuarded`/`openShipItDialog`; on confirm, `executeResolvedCommand(SHIP_IT_COMMAND, state, opts.onCommand, frozen, model, opts.onDowntimeToggle, undefined, opts.onRefresh)`; `dispatchChordCommand` routes `/skill:ship` → `resolveAndRouteCommand` → `onCommand(command, model, ...)` (paneTitle = selected item's title, focus undefined).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand` agent route: `interactiveItemId = extractWorkItemId(command)` → `undefined` for ship → `resolveInteractiveItemAnchorAfterAdmission` returns `null` → `--anchor` omitted → `send-to-pi.sh` splits the current pane (current tab).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor(cwd, workspaceId, itemId, ...)` wraps `getItemTabAnchor`; fails open to `null` (current-pane split) on any error; supports `'left-of-extensions'` placement.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor` creates-or-reuses a tab whose label is the key.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — `runShipGuard`/`formatBlockedNotice` gate ship entry on live panes carrying project work-item IDs (blocked-notice UI already exists to reuse for the second-command rejection).

## Desired change

1. In the interactive agent dispatch path (`index.ts` `onCommand`), when the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` (`/skill:ship release`), resolve the interactive tab anchor with the literal label **`Ship`** instead of the (missing) work-item ID — reusing `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`/`getItemTabAnchor` so the tab is created on first use and reused thereafter. Forward the anchor's pane id to `send-to-pi.sh` via `--anchor`, producing a pi pane inside the `Ship` tab.
2. Use `'left-of-extensions'` placement for a freshly created `Ship` tab (a reused tab is never moved).
3. Pass `focus: true` on the ship dispatch so the release pane is focused/zoomed on open.
4. Extend the ship-entry gate so a second Ship command is rejected while the first release is active: the guard (or a lightweight check on the same `shipGuardQuery` pane data) treats a live pane in the `Ship` tab as blocking — show the existing blocked notice, never open the confirmation dialog.
5. Fail-open: any anchor resolution/creation failure keeps today's current-pane split.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — the `onCommand` agent route: substitute the `Ship` label for the item-ID anchor lookup, forward `--anchor` + `--focus`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` (reused; may need a label param or ship-specific caller).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — ship dialog dispatch (`openShipItDialog.*`, `executeResolvedCommand` call), second-command rejection gate wiring, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — extend guard result to include a live `Ship`-tab pane as a blocking condition (rejection path).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` / `.herdr-cli.ts` — existing `getItemTabAnchor` / `createTabInWorkspace` reused unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `S` shortcut entry (unchanged unless focus/code_freeze policy changes).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog-tui.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard-tui.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Title/requirement wording**: the item title says "own pane" but the requirement (and operator's confirmation) is an own *tab* labelled `Ship`; the pane inside the tab is the pi session. Implementation should key on the tab, not a pane rename.
- **Second-command rejection signal**: "first release still active" is interpreted as *a live pi pane in the `Ship` tab* (from the same `shipGuardQuery` pane list). If pane-liveness cannot be determined (query failure), fail safe the same way the existing guard does (blocked notice) — never open a second release.
- **Scope creep**: embedding extra capacity work in this item is out of scope — record as linked work items if discovered (e.g. a "reuse completed Ship tab" toggle, per-workspace Ship tabs, pane renaming policy).
- **Assumption**: placement, focus and rejection apply to the interactive `S` shortcut dispatch path only; other `/skill:ship` invocations keep current behaviour unless the same code path is shared.

## Related work

- WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY — Ship It shortcut + typed confirmation dialog (parent requirement: dispatch path).
- WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW — code freeze on ship confirmation + ship guard semantics (extension point for the second-command rejection).
- WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS — Pi processes start in a work-item tab (the item-ID tab machinery this item reuses with a fixed `Ship` label).
- WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW / WL-0MW5E5V20002T0KW — left-of-extensions tab placement (fresh-tab placement policy).
- WL-0MUDEGBGO00609RV — ship-guard pure module (guard extension point).

## Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0ML5YRMB11GQV4HR** – Slash Command Palette (completed)
- **WL-0MSG6ZI3D003VYZZ** – Fix resize-mode anchor resolution: herdr pane current rejects --json (completed)
- **WL-0MTR2HLLJ009PTPJ** – Wire pane spawn to use persisted dispatcher anchor (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `CLI.md`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/herdr/README.md`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Tab lifecycle — should a second Ship command reuse an existing 'Ship' tab, or always open a fresh tab?" — Answer (operator): "A second ship command while the first is still active should be rejected." — Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: one release at a time — the `Ship` tab is created on first use and reused, and a second Ship command while the first release is active is blocked (never a fresh tab, never a second pane in the same tab). Prior options offered/rejected: reuse the tab (preferred at the time) vs fresh tab each time (rejected — would allow concurrent releases).
- Q2: "Where should a freshly created 'Ship' tab be placed?" — Answer (operator): **A — left-of-extensions** (same placement as interactive item-ID tabs, WL-0MW5E5V20002T0KW). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the Ship pane take focus when it opens?" — Answer (operator): **B — focus the Ship pane** so the operator immediately sees the release run. Source: interactive reply. Note: current behaviour is `--no-focus`; this item changes it for the Ship dispatch only.

## Problem

`tests/**` resolve `@worklog/shared` through the package `exports` map to the **built** output (`packages/shared/dist/`), which is gitignored. A checkout whose `packages/shared/dist` predates a change under `packages/shared/src` therefore exercises the OLD shared code, and the full suite reports failures for work that is already correct and merged.

Each implement worktree builds its own `packages/shared/dist`, so the dev-push gate (which tests the pushed commit in a clean/wt checkout) can be green while the long-lived main checkout stays stale — the failure then reappears in the main checkout, in audit runs and in any agent session that runs the suite from there.

## Evidence (2026-11-08)

- Main checkout `packages/shared/dist/database/work-items.js` was built 2026-11-07T13:46Z; commit `36d965a4` (WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7, 2026-11-08T21:22Z) changed `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts` to add cascade delete attribution.
- A fresh full-suite run at dev HEAD `3dad96d4` (clean tree, `run_tests.py --type full --scope full --force`) failed 3 tests in `tests/cli/delete-reason.test.ts`: expected `cascade from <parent-id>: sweeping subtree`, received `sweeping subtree` (the pre-change behaviour).
- After `npm run build` in the same checkout the identical suite was green: 344 files / 4825 tests passed, 0 failed.

## Desired outcome

Make the mismatch visible instead of silent, e.g. any of:

- a guard that fails the suite (or `run_tests.py`) with an actionable message when `packages/shared/src` is newer than `packages/shared/dist`;
- a build step in the test runner for the workspace shared package (cost-aware, cache-keyed);
- a documented, enforced rebuild precondition for full-suite evidence in `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` / the test-skill reference.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-suite run in a checkout with a `packages/shared/dist` older than `packages/shared/src` either rebuilds it or fails immediately with an actionable message naming the rebuild command.
2. The guard/behaviour is covered by a test (stale and fresh dist cases).
3. `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (and the test-skill reference if behaviour lives in the runner) document the requirement.
4. The full project test suite passes.

## Impact

Agents and audits stop chasing phantom test failures caused by a stale local workspace build, so a red suite once again means the code is actually broken.

# Decide: remove the own-backlog fallback (and its leadership step-down) now that dispatch covers the whole backlog?

**Type:** decision / cleanup. **Priority:** low. **Raised by:** WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH.

## Why this exists

WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH ("Dispatcher selection must consider every work item, not just the sprint view") removed the sprint-view-only dispatch window. Every path now walks the **whole ranked backlog**, not just the rendered `browseItemCount` window.

That change silently altered the premise of the **own-backlog fallback** added by WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 (and its `dispatched-from-own-backlog-detected` tag and its leadership step-down of WL-0MUZPBRX3007STFK). That fallback existed to give the leader a **bounded, privileged escape valve** into its own *hidden* backlog when the offer list yielded nothing — and to relinquish leadership afterwards so no instance could monopolise the role by repeatedly reaching into hidden work.

With the whole backlog now offerable and dispatchable by every instance, there is **no hidden backlog**, so there is no privilege to grant, and the monopolisation premise the step-down defends against no longer exists for this path. The code still runs, still carries a `dispatched-from-own-backlog-detected` path in tests, and still forces a leadership hand-off — which now arguably *hurts* throughput: the leader gives up leadership for dispatching ordinary visible work.

**This work item asks for a decision, not an implementation.** Options are recorded below; the outcome should be recorded here and then either removed, retained with a documented rationale, or re-scoped.

## The code path (complete)

### Entry point

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `dispatchFromCoordination()`:

1. **Line 688-701** — the `// ── Own-backlog fallback (parent WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 AC1–AC9) ──` comment block.
2. **Line 732** — `const ownWindow = await readOwnHeadWindow(deps, opts.cwd, opts.browseItemCount);` — reads the leader's OWN root only.
3. **Lines 738-761** — **audit-batch continuation** branch: `dispatchFromOwnHead(... selectionReason: 'own-backlog-audit-batch-continuation' ...)`, only when `batchRemainingBefore > 0 && batchCap > 1` and `kinds: ['audit']`.
4. **Lines 770-788** — **the registered-root sweep** (`dispatchFromRegisteredRoots`) runs *before* the own-backlog fallback. Unrelated to this decision but shares the same window helper and the same terminal-reason composition.
5. **Lines 791-818** — **the own-backlog fallback itself**: `dispatchFromOwnHead(... selectionReason: 'own-backlog-fallback', kinds: null, includeHead: false ...)`.
6. **Line 810** — `if (ownOutcome.dispatched) return { ...ownOutcome, ownBacklogDispatch: true };` — the flag that triggers the step-down.

### Supporting code

| Location | Role |
|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.head-scan.ts:201` | `dispatchFromOwnHead()` — the shared sequential filter chain. `includeHead: false` scans **only `tail`** (the extension beyond the sprint window). |
| `downtime-worker.head-scan.ts:211` | `const ranked = ctx.includeHead ? [...head, ...tail] : tail;` — the own-backlog fallback therefore scans only the *out-of-view tail*. |
| `downtime-worker.head-scan.ts:370` | `dispatchFromRegisteredRoots()` — the sweep (separate concern). |
| `downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts:83` | `readOwnHeadWindow()` — `getHerdrListHead(cwd, sprintWindow)` + `fetchWholeBacklogTail()`. **Changed by WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH:** the tail is now the WHOLE backlog, not one bounded step. |
| `downtime-worker.gates.ts:807` | `fetchWholeBacklogTail()` — loops `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` until exhausted (geometric growth, `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS = 20` cap). |
| `downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts:482` | `ownBacklogDispatch?: boolean` — the outcome surface. |
| `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:211` | Audit-batch: `ownBacklogDispatch: finalized.dispatched && batchEnded` — the batch defers the hand-off to batch end. |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:853-856` | The consumer: `if (outcome.ownBacklogDispatch === true && ctx.leaderManager !== null) { ctx.leaderManager.releaseLeadership(); ctx.leaderState = false; }` |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:891-902` | The **separate** empty-cycle step-down (`WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A`) — reuses `releaseLeadership()`, NOT the `ownBacklogDispatch` flag. Out of scope but easy to conflate; do not remove it with this decision. |

### Tests that pin the current behaviour

| Test | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` ~2852 | `step-down surface AC1: a successful own-backlog dispatch flags ownBacklogDispatch` |
| `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` ~2870 | `step-down surface AC2: a normal in-view (offer-list) dispatch does NOT flag ownBacklogDispatch` |
| `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` ~2894 | `step-down surface AC3: when the fallback finds no eligible item no step-down is surfaced` |
| `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` ~2547-2800 | `own-backlog fallback — leader selection contract (WL-0MUZPBQQ3001DAM6)` — AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC9 incl. the window-shape test rewritten by WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH |
| `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` ~2850-2960 | audit-batch continuation + `ownBacklogDispatch` deferred to batch end |
| `coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts` ~406 | sweep dispatch does NOT raise `ownBacklogDispatch` |
| `integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts` ~481 | **Rewritten by WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH:** now asserts an out-of-view item is a normal fleet-visible OFFER and does **not** step down. The fallback+step-down integration case is no longer reachable and was replaced with an explanatory note. |

## Reachability analysis — is it dead code?

**Not strictly dead, but substantially narrowed.** The fallback still runs when the offer scan dispatches nothing, and it can still dispatch because `readOwnHeadWindow` now returns the *whole* backlog as `tail`. Cases where it can still fire:

| # | Scenario | Still reachable? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Leader's own offer was removed at dispatch time (stale/gated) and its *next* item is dispatchable | **Yes** | The offer carries ONE item (`computeMostImportantItem` → `workItemId`); the fallback walks the rest. This is the strongest remaining case. |
| R2 | Leader's own offer is held by a gate the owner did not apply (review-queue depth, CPU gate, code-freeze) while another own item passes | **Partly** | The leader keeps the entry for holds but proceeds to the fallback; `dispatchFromOwnHead` re-applies the same filters. |
| R3 | Audit batch armed and the continuation target lies beyond the head | **Yes** | `own-backlog-audit-batch-continuation`, `kinds: ['audit']` only. |
| R4 | No coordination entries at all (single instance, or all peers dead) | **Yes** | The leader's own offer is written at check-in, so this needs the entry to be absent/removed. |
| R5 | The original premise: offer list empty because the sprint view was empty but the backlog had work | **No** | Killed by WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH — the offer now covers the whole backlog. |

So the honest reading: the fallback is **redundant as a "hidden backlog" valve (R5 gone)** but **still a "second chance within one tick" mechanism (R1-R4 live)**, particularly for the audit-batch continuation.

## Decision variables

Record the answer to each here when deciding.

| # | Variable | Options | Current state |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Is the fallback removed, retained, or re-scoped?** | (a) remove entirely; (b) retain as-is; (c) retain R1-R4 but drop the `ownBacklogDispatch` step-down; (d) collapse into the registered-root sweep | unresolved |
| D2 | **Does the leadership step-down still serve a purpose?** | keep / drop / keep only for the audit-batch continuation | The monopolisation premise (hidden backlog) is gone. Dropping it *increases* throughput but removes a fairness guard that is cheap to keep. |
| D3 | **Does `ownBacklogDispatch` remain a meaningful outcome surface?** | keep / rename (it no longer means "own backlog") / remove | Its name is now misleading: it fires for work that is fleet-visible. |
| D4 | **What is the audit-batch continuation's fate?** | keep (independent of the fallback) / fold into the same decision | R3 is genuinely exercised; it is the strongest argument for retention. |
| D5 | **Is the round-robin cursor sufficient fairness?** | yes (leadership fairness owned by `selectLeastRecentlyServed`) / no | WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH documentation asserts yes. |
| D6 | **Legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`)** | unaffected? | `leaderManager === null` ⇒ step-down never fires; the direct path now dispatches the whole backlog. |
| D7 | **Empty-cycle step-down (`WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A`)** | keep (independent) | Separate arm, separate rationale; must NOT be removed with this decision. |
| D8 | **Test churn** | how many to rewrite/delete | 3 step-down surface tests + the leader selection contract block + the integration case already rewritten. |
| D9 | **Documentation** | `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` sections *Own-backlog fallback & leadership hand-off* and *No-candidate cooldown* | already reconciled by WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH to say the fallback is a no-dispatchable-offer case |
| D10 | **Performance** | cost of `readOwnHeadWindow` walking the whole tail on every no-answer tick | geometric growth + round cap; measured cold `wl worklist -n 200` ≈ 3.4 s, warm ≈ 0.2 s (read cache). A removal saves one window walk per empty tick. |
| D11 | **Blast radius if removed** | what else consumes `dispatchFromOwnHead` | the audit-batch continuation and the registered-root sweep. Removing the fallback must not remove those. |
| D12 | **Reversibility / risk** | low — pure removal, well covered | all paths are unit-tested; the sweep and continuation are independent call sites. |

## Recommendation (for the decider to accept or reject)

**Option (c)**: retain the mechanism for R1-R4 (especially the audit-batch continuation), but **drop the `ownBacklogDispatch` step-down** and rename the surface, or fold the fallback into the registered-root sweep so there is one "scan my own root's remaining backlog" path rather than two. Rationale: the step-down's fairness premise is gone, so keeping it only costs throughput; the scan itself is still the cheapest way to use a tick when every offer is stale.

If the decider prefers **(a) remove entirely**, the audit-batch continuation and the registered-root sweep must be preserved — they share `dispatchFromOwnHead`, not the fallback block.

## Acceptance criteria (for whichever option is chosen)

1. The decision and its rationale are recorded in this work item, answering D1-D12.
2. If removed: the `own-backlog-fallback` block (`coordination-leader.ts:688-701, 791-818`), the `ownBacklogDispatch` field (`dispatch-contract.ts:482`) and its consumer (`orchestrator-dispatch.ts:853-856`) are gone; the audit-batch continuation (`:738-761`) and the registered-root sweep (`:770-788`) still work and are still tested.
3. If retained with a changed step-down: `ownBacklogDispatch` (or its replacement) no longer fires for fleet-visible work, and the audit-batch deferral (`coordination-leader.ts:211`) stays consistent.
4. The empty-cycle step-down (`orchestrator-dispatch.ts:891-902`, `WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A`) is untouched and still tested.
5. `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts` and `integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts` are updated to the decided contract — no test silently deleted, each change explained in a comment.
6. `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (*Own-backlog fallback & leadership hand-off*) matches the decision.
7. Full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` (688-701, 732, 738-761, 770-788, 791-818, 211)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` (201-215, 370)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts` (83)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` (807)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-contract.ts` (482, 511)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` (853-856, 891-902)
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `coordination-registered-root-sweep.test.ts`, `integration-leader-dispatch.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

## Impact

The dispatcher carries a leadership hand-off whose original justification (a privileged view of a hidden backlog) no longer exists; deciding its fate removes either dead complexity or a throughput cost, and leaves the dispatcher's documented contract matching its actual behaviour.

# Host-wide release barrier while a release runs

## Problem statement

The Code Freeze marker (`.worklog/code-freeze.json`) is **per worklog root**, but the host dispatch budget ledger is **machine-scoped**. During a release in project A the dispatcher skips new implement/audit dispatch for project A only; another project on the same host (or the coordination leader's registered-root sweep) can still start implement/audit panes while the release's own audit/test subprocesses are saturating the machine.

The release-dispatch-budget evaluation (WL-0MW7YIBG70021YI3) concluded a dedicated release *budget slot* is not warranted (the ledger counts dispatched panes, not release subprocesses), but identified this cross-project scope mismatch as the real residual gap.

## Proposed change

Introduce a machine-scoped release-in-progress marker (in `machine-coordination.ts`, alongside the budget ledger — reusing the same coordination dir/lock) that the dispatcher honours for **implement and audit** tiers on **every root**, so a release anywhere on the host pauses new heavy dispatch everywhere. In-progress panes keep running; plan/intake prep still dispatches (matching the per-root freeze split-by-skill).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A machine-scoped release marker is written/cleared by the release process with the same atomic + fail-closed semantics as `code-freeze.json`.
2. While the marker is active, the dispatcher skips new implement/audit dispatch for every root (both the direct path and the coordination-leader sweep), with a neutral reason token that does not arm the no-candidate cooldown.
3. In-progress implement/audit panes are not interrupted; plan/intake (including critical prep) still dispatches.
4. The per-root code-freeze gate remains and composes with the host barrier (belt-and-braces).
5. The ledger's admission path stays unchanged for budget accounting; this barrier is a separate, earlier gate.
6. Documentation and tests pin the behaviour.

## Related work

- WL-0MW7YIBG70021YI3 — Evaluate budgets (parent evaluation; recommends this follow-up)

# F2 — Generic admission + audit-only over-hold

Second implementation slice of WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB: make admission one generic
path for every capped kind on BOTH dispatcher paths (direct and coordination
leader), keep the counting asymmetry audit-only (`freshCount` over-hold for
audit; `liveCount` live-pane release for every other kind), and unify refusal
tokens on `host-budget-<kind>` (removing the `maxAudit: 1` → `audit-host-saturated`
special-case). Uncapped kinds admit without reservation and touch no ledger.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `admitHostDispatch` resolves the kind's cap from the generalised config:
  absent ⇒ admit WITHOUT reservation (no reserve/release/confirm bookkeeping);
  present ⇒ existing live-count admission; `0` ⇒ refuse with `0/0`.
- Counting asymmetry preserved: only `audit` uses `freshCount` (slot held from
  reservation until a release point or the 2 h stale window, no live-pane
  requirement); `implement`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort` use `liveCount`
  (live-pane release, pane-derived freshness).
- Admission is enforced on BOTH dispatcher paths: the direct path
  (`dispatchClaimedTier` in `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`) and the
  coordination-leader path (`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` /
  `coordination-batch.ts`) call the same generic `admitHostDispatch` for every
  capped kind and skip it for uncapped kinds.
- Refusal tokens unified: `host-budget-<kind>` for the kind's cap refusal;
  `audit-host-saturated` special-case removed (the audit tier reports
  `host-budget-audit` at every cap including the `maxAudit: 1` default).
- Fail-closed semantics unchanged: unreadable ledger ⇒ `host-budget-unknown` +
  repair from live panes; `no-coordination-dir` ⇒ admit; lock/IO failure ⇒ refuse.
- `kindOf`/`entriesFromLivePanes` reconstruct any kind's pane (not just
  implement/audit) for the repair path.

- **Traceability (covers parent AC1 — any kind configurable):** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the per-kind kill switch.
- **Traceability (covers parent AC4 — counting asymmetry preserved, audit-only):** only `audit` keeps the over-hold semantics: it counts fresh ledger entries with **no** live-pane requirement (`freshCount` — slot held from reservation until a release point fires or the 2 h stale window). Every **other** kind counts only fresh entries whose pane is in the machine-wide live pane list (`liveCount`), so its slot frees when the pane leaves the live list.
## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission,
  refusal tokens, audit over-hold, repair
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — admission choke
  point (`dispatchClaimedTier`) + failure release for all kinds
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` —
  `dispatchFromCoordination` admission
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `admitHostDispatch` seam (kind passthrough)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.test.ts` /
  `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` / `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`

## Minimal Implementation

1. Generalise `admitHostDispatch` to look up the kind's cap/absence.
2. Add the no-reservation fast path for uncapped kinds.
3. Remove the `audit-host-saturated` special-case in `readAuditBudgetState` /
   `admitAuditLegacy`; unify on `host-budget-audit`.
4. Generalise `kindOf` / `entriesFromLivePanes` for pane-title reconstruction.
5. Widen `releaseHostBudgetForFailure` and the admission call in
   `dispatchClaimedTier` to all kinds (skip still for uncapped — release is a
   no-op for kinds that never reserve).
6. Update admission/dispatch/coordination tests; run the changed-scope gate.

## Dependencies

- F1 (WL-0MWF33ZB0000RC88) — generalised config/ledger.
- T1 (WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E) — the test matrix pins admission semantics.

One generic admission path; audit-only over-hold; unified tokens; both
dispatcher paths enforce caps for every configured kind.

# Coordination file never prunes dead-instance entries, so stale offers are re-fetched every tick

## Problem statement

`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json` (v2) accumulates one entry per
herdr instance and nothing ever removes the entry of an instance that has
stopped existing. Only two paths remove an entry: a dispatch-time rejection
(`removeOffer` → entry dropped when its last offer goes) and an instance
removing its own entry on an empty offer window. A crashed or killed instance
does neither, so its entry — and its offers — persist forever.

Live evidence (13 Nov 2026, 22:18 UTC, `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`):

| instanceId | worklogRoot | lastUpdated | offers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `8bde6002` | `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising` | 09:02:13 | (implement, **RISE-0MW7V58ZP0058NMI**) |
| `f003722b` | `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents` | 09:06:43 | (implement, **SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I**) |
| `fcb61c9b` | `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising` | 22:15:12 | (audit, RISE-0MW7V58ZP0058NMI) |
| `5da23429` | `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` | 22:15:34 | (prep, WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN) |
| `a242103a` | `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents` | 22:16:37 | (audit, SA-0MWA7OD8O001945I) |
| `c64f7fb9` | `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell` | 22:16:55 | (implement + audit) |
| `8f416178` | `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street` | 22:17:09 | (audit) |
| `4a56071f` | `/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine` | 22:18:02 | (audit) |

Two entries are 13 h stale (the check-in cadence is 5 min and the leader lease
TTL is 5 min), and both roots appear twice as a result. Both stale offers also
advertise a *kind* that is no longer correct: those items have since moved to
`completed`/`in_review`, so the classifier now resolves them as `audit` while
the entry still says `implement`.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want `downtime-coordination.json` to contain only live
  herdr instances, so the file I read to judge instance health is trustworthy.
- **As an agent debugging dispatch behaviour**, I do not want to chase offers
  from instances that stopped existing hours ago.
- **As the operator paying for idle ticks**, I do not want a wasted
  `wl show` + classify subprocess per dead entry on every dispatch tick.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An entry whose `lastUpdated` is older than a bounded staleness window is removed from the machine coordination file on the **leader's check-in path**, and the removal is logged as one coordination-log record per pruned entry naming that entry's `instanceId`, `worklogRoot` and last-seen timestamp (`operation: 'prune'`).
- The default staleness window is a multiple of the **check-in cadence** (`DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS`, 5 min) — 2 × cadence (10 min) — so one missed check-in is tolerated; it is clamped (minimum 1 × cadence, maximum 24 h) and overridable via a settings key following the `downtimeMarkerStaleWindowMs` pattern.
- Pruning is fail-open: an unreadable/corrupt file, a lock-contended prune or a write failure never blocks a dispatch and never throws out of the tick — the prune is skipped and retried on the next tick.
- Pruning never removes a live entry: an entry refreshed within the window survives unchanged, and when nothing is stale the file is not rewritten at all (byte-identical, no-op).
- Duplicate entries for one `worklogRoot` resolve deterministically: only stale duplicates are pruned, the freshest live entry and its offers are untouched, and `entryRoots` therefore contains no root twice for a dead/live pair.
- The existing non-expiring offer contract is preserved: offers of a **live** instance never expire by age (they still persist until dispatched or dropped by the dispatch-time eligibility check), and `hasPeerOffer`'s 24 h liveness predicate is unchanged.
- Tests cover: (a) one live + one stale entry → only the live one remains after a tick; (b) a stale duplicate for a root that also has a live entry → stale pruned, live offers intact; (c) a corrupt/unreadable file → left untouched, tick proceeds; (d) the prune is idempotent (second tick prunes nothing, no write); (e) a live-but-idle instance (no offers, refreshed within the window) is never pruned.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the staleness window, its default/clamp/settings key, the prune trigger (leader check-in), the log record shape, and how this coexists with the retired wall-clock TTL prune (`WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The dispatcher rotates over live instances only, so dead projects stop consuming rotation slots and no dispatch tick spends a `wl show` on work that can never be dispatched.

## Constraints

- No new npm dependency; the coordination path stays dependency-free.
- The prune is leader-only and happens inside the existing `withCoordLock` read-modify-write, never as a separate unlocked pass.
- Do not re-introduce offer expiry: only entries that stop checking in are pruned. A live instance's offers keep the non-expiring contract.
- Coordination log stays bounded by the existing rolling policy (one record per pruned entry, not per tick).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — `pruneStaleEntries` is a documented no-op (`WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P`); `removeOffer` / `removeEntry` are the only removals; `upsertEntry` / `mergeEntries` are lock-guarded read-modify-write.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — the check-in write path (`current` entry read, `removeEntry` on an empty window, `upsertEntry` on a fresh offer).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — builds `entryRoots` from every entry with offers (dead entries included) and walks entries in file order.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — `CoordinationLogEntry` already carries an unused `prunedCount` field plus `instanceId`/`operation`/`reason`.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Lifecycle 3 ("Pruning — retired") and the `hasPeerOffer` liveness note document the current, deliberately non-expiring behaviour.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS` (5 min), `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` (24 h).

## Desired change

1. Add a `pruneDeadEntries(coordDir, { nowMs, staleWindowMs, leaderInstanceId })` (name to be finalised at plan time) in `coordination.ts`: one lock-held read → filter entries whose `lastUpdated` is unparseable or older than the window → write only if anything was removed → return the pruned entries. Fail-open on every error path.
2. Call it once per leader check-in/tick from the leader path (not from followers), before offers are used, so `entryRoots` and the entry walk in the same tick see the pruned set.
3. Log one `operation: 'prune'` coordination record per pruned entry carrying `instanceId`, `worklogRoot`, `lastSeen` (`lastUpdated`), the window used and `reason: 'staleness-window'`.
4. Add the settings key with clamp + default derived from the check-in cadence, wire it into the worker config the way `downtimeMarkerStaleWindowMs` is wired.
5. Update the docs section that currently declares pruning retired, stating the new dead-entry-only rule and what still never expires.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — new `pruneDeadEntries` beside `removeOffer` / `removeEntry`; header comment for the retired `pruneStaleEntries` no-op must be reconciled.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — leader-only call site (AC: prune on the leader check-in path).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — confirm `entryRoots` de-duplication follows from the prune; comment currently says "No wall-clock prune".
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — log record fields for the prune (`prunedCount` + per-entry `instanceId`/`worklogRoot`/`lastSeen`).
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — new `downtimeCoordinationEntryStaleMs`-style key, clamp, default from the cadence.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts` — tests (a)–(e).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — staleness window, trigger, log shape, reconciliation with the retired TTL prune.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Contradicts a retired decision unless stated precisely.** `WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P` / `WL-0MTOBZZNU0009MW1` removed wall-clock entry expiry, and `WL-0MTOC1CHO007TXCL` documented "entries do not expire". The distinction this item relies on: a *live* instance re-checks in every 5 min, so its entry never reaches the window; only an owner that stopped running does. Mitigation: the docs AC requires stating that rule explicitly, and AC "live instance's offers never expire" pins it in tests.
- **Window too tight would prune live followers.** Default must be ≥ 2 × check-in cadence, not 2 × lease TTL, because followers keep no lease and refresh only on the check-in cadence. Recorded as an assumption; the configurable/clamped key bounds operator error.
- **Write amplification / lock contention.** Prune adds one lock-held read-modify-write per leader tick. Mitigated by the no-write-when-nothing-stale rule and fail-open skip; the existing `upsertEntry` path already takes the same lock per tick.
- **Log flooding.** One record per pruned entry; a mass instance death could add N records in one tick. Bounded by entry count and the rolling coordination log policy; acceptable, and it is exactly the evidence an operator wants.
- **Scope creep — duplicate-root rotation.** Duplicate roots in `entryRoots` (and `selectLeastRecentlyServed` seeing a root twice) are a *symptom* of ghosts. If live-vs-live duplicates are still observed after this lands, that is a separate item (different cause: two live instances on one root), not scope here.
- Assumption: dead instances never need their entry preserved for audit — the coordination log carries the forensic record, so pruning the file loses nothing.

## Related work

Potentially related work items (see the automated report appended after this section for the ranked list):

- `WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P` — "Remove coordination entry expiry; validate eligibility at dispatch time" (completed) — the decision being qualified.
- `WL-0MTOBZZNU0009MW1` — "Remove coordination TTL prune" (completed) — same decision, per-checkpoint ACs.
- `WL-0MTOC1CHO007TXCL` — "Docs: non-expiring coordination contract" (completed) — the doc section to amend.
- `WL-0MTOC12CR000NULW` — "Dispatch validates eligibility at dispatch time" (completed) — the replacement gate that stays authoritative.
- `WL-0MSXH9UT6008151F` — "Implement shared coordination file module" (completed) — `coordination.ts` ownership.
- `WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y` — liveness-aware `hasPeerOffer` (24 h window) — the read-side liveness predicate to keep unchanged.
- `WL-0MTMPSCL8000O45H` — check-in cadence (5 min) and immediate re-offer behaviour — the cadence the default window derives from.
- `WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK` — round-robin `selectLeastRecentlyServed` wiring — the consumer of `entryRoots`.

Potentially related docs:

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — lifecycle, `hasPeerOffer` liveness note, "Pruning — retired".
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — header contract for the v2 file and the non-expiring note.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — downtime/coordination section mirrors the contract.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Session: intake run in a herdr-driven (non-interactive) agent session, 13 Nov 2026; no producer present to answer, so both questions are recorded as **OPEN QUESTION** with the assumption actually used, to be confirmed by the producer at review.

- **Q1: Which cadence should the staleness window default to — lease TTL or check-in cadence?** — **OPEN QUESTION** (no interactive producer). Assumption used: 2 × `DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS` (10 min), clamped [1 × cadence, 24 h], configurable. Rationale: followers hold no lease and refresh only on the check-in cadence, so a lease-TTL-derived window would prune live followers; `DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_SECONDS` and the check-in cadence are both 5 min today, so the two values coincide at the default and only the semantics differ. Evidence: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts:806`, `packages/herdr/src/leader-election.ts:42`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Lifecycle 1. **Recommended:** derive from the check-in cadence — it is the signal every instance actually emits.
- **Q2: Does pruning dead entries contradict the retired wall-clock TTL prune (`WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P`)?** — **OPEN QUESTION** (no interactive producer). Assumption used: no contradiction in intent — that decision removed expiry of *live* offers (which starved dispatch); this item removes entries whose owner stopped running. Live entries are refreshed every 5 min and can never reach a 10 min window, so the non-expiring offer contract holds. Evidence: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Lifecycle 3; `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts:753` (`pruneStaleEntries` no-op). **Recommended:** accept the distinction and pin it with the AC "a live instance's offers never expire".

Research summary: repo and worklog searches found the retired-prune decisions plus the liveness-aware read predicate and the check-in cadence; the live coordination file confirmed exactly two 13-hour-stale entries (one per duplicated root) and the stale-offer kind mismatch (`implement` advertised for items now classified `audit`).

dependency order. Each item is deliverable as its own end-to-end slice (code +
tests where applicable) so the tree stays buildable between items.

| 3 | `WL-0MWFJTULD005DTQI` — Settings key for coordination entry staleness | feature | `downtimeCoordinationEntryStaleMs` default `2 × DEFAULT_COORDINATION_CHECK_IN_MS`, clamped `[1 × cadence, 24 h]`, wired settings → worker config → prune. |
| 4 | `WL-0MWFJU3NC009H7JB` — Docs: dead-entry staleness window and prune | docs | `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §Lifecycle 3 + `hasPeerOffer` note + timings table row, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and the `coordination.ts` header comment reconciled with the retired TTL prune. |

# Downtime offers: fill empty buckets from the rest of the project backlog, not just the visible list

## Problem statement

The dispatcher can only dispatch what an instance *offers*, but each herdr instance computes its offers in `computeMostImportantItem` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) by partitioning its **sprint-view window only** — the live `browseItemCount`, currently 20 items — into the `implement` / `audit` / `prep` buckets. A bucket that yields no nominee inside that window nominates nothing, and the window is deliberately never widened to fill it (WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P AC3). The existing whole-backlog extension (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `fetchWholeBacklogTail`, WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH) feeds only the *single* legacy offer, never the nominee buckets.

Live evidence from 13 Nov 2026 (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`):

```
AI_Hell              offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
ContextHub           offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
tce-the-rising       offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
SorraAgents          offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
tce-main-street      offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
Tableau-Card-Engine  offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
```

`tce-the-rising`'s ranked head is three `plan_complete` items followed by 16 `in_review` audits; the first two plan items are filtered out (a 24 h dispatched marker and a live pane). The window's audit bucket therefore fills, the other buckets nominate nothing, and the leader has no prep or implement offer to fall through to when the audit is refused. Its backlog beyond item 20 — and every other ready item in the project — is invisible to the dispatcher.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want each project's ready work to be reachable by the dispatcher even when it sits below the visible worklist, so projects with large backlogs stop appearing idle.
- **As an agent debugging a root that offers only audits**, I want the offer computation to explain that it widened, or that every candidate was gated.

### User stories

1. When `tce-the-rising`'s visible top 20 items contain only audits, its check-in advertises an `implement` and a `prep` nominee drawn from items 21+, so the leader has a fall-through when the audit is refused.
2. When the leader refuses an audit for the entered entry, the same entry's `prep` nominee is dispatched in the same tick (no re-offer round trip).
3. When a deeper candidate is gated (producer-review flag, dispatched marker, in-flight pane, review-queue hold), it never becomes a nominee merely because the scan went deeper.
4. When a root genuinely has nothing dispatchable in its whole backlog, the outcome is the same `noCandidate` result with the same attribution as before.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The nominee scan is no longer window-only: for each `implement` / `audit` / `prep` bucket without a nominee after the visible window is scanned, the scan continues through the geometric whole-backlog extension (reuse the existing loop over `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` growth and `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS` cap; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` is the same primitive wrapped to exhaustion and is used by the batch path, not by this function) until that bucket has a nominee or the tail is exhausted.
- The extension is a WINDOW WIDENING of the same canonical ranking (`getHerdrListHead`), never a second ranking and never a second `wl` spawn per bucket: one read path, buckets partitioned from the same ordered stream.
- Every sequential filter is applied unchanged to extended candidates: classification (producer-review gate, freshness/recency, risk/effort caps), dispatched-marker exclusion (24 h TTL), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze split-by-skill, in-flight guard, and the review-queue depth hold. No filter is relaxed or reordered, and a gate-held candidate never becomes a nominee just because it is deeper.
- Cost is bounded and observable: the extension only runs when a bucket is unfilled, growth is geometric, rounds are capped, and the existing fail-open behaviour holds (an absent/`{ok:false}`/throwing extension leaves the pre-change result byte-identical and never blocks dispatch).
- A `nomineesFilledBeyondWindow` (or equivalent) signal is recorded on the check-in / decision-log entry naming which buckets needed the extension and how many extra items were read, so an operator can see a root being reached past its visible list.
- Tests (added to `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` and any new sibling): (a) a 20-item window whose buckets are fully gated but whose tail holds one eligible `plan` and one eligible `implement` yields both nominees, in canonical order; (b) after a refused audit the same entry still dispatches its prep nominee — the fall-through the leader's phase-2 ladder already supports; (c) a tail with nothing eligible still resolves `noCandidate` with unchanged attribution; (d) the extension is not entered when the window already fills every bucket (no extra reads); (e) a `wl` failure in the extension leaves the window result unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states that the visible window bounds rendering only, and that buckets are filled from the whole ranked backlog — the "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" paragraph is rewritten accordingly, and the "window is never widened to fill a bucket" statements in `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` (and the AC3 note in `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`) are updated.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- **Explicitly out of scope, recorded rather than silently absorbed:** (i) candidates held by the 24 h dispatched-marker or by a still-open in-flight pane stay invisible regardless of widening — separate items own those (they are why `RISE-0MWC9J1OD001CT26` and `RISE-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG` are not offered today); (ii) the leader's registered-root sweep (`downtimeWorklogRoots`) stays a separate, independent mechanism; (iii) the audit-admission budget fix and the round-robin charge are separate items — this change must not touch either.

## Impact

Every project can offer its dispatcher a full set of buckets drawn from its whole backlog, so a root whose visible top 20 items are all audits no longer hands the leader an empty menu while its ready work waits below the fold.

## Constraints

- One read path: bucket partitioning and the single offer must come from the same ordered stream produced by `getHerdrListHead`; no per-bucket `wl` spawn and no second ranking implementation.
- Filter order is load-bearing (it decides attribution and side effects such as `flagBudgetExhausted`); the extension must run the same `scanOfferable` chain unchanged, only over more items.
- Extra reads are paid only when needed: no widening when the window already fills every bucket, and the walk stops as soon as all buckets are filled.
- Fail-open is non-negotiable: an extension that fails or adds nothing must leave the pre-change result byte-identical (same `noCandidate` / hold tokens and attribution).
- Backwards compatibility: entries whose nominees are all window-sourced stay byte-identical; v1-era leaders keep reading `workItemId` as the first offer.
- Run-time budget: the leader tick cost must stay within the existing benchmark ceiling (`npm run benchmark:leader-tick-cost`), since the entry may now carry nominees sourced from more reads on the owner side.

## Existing state

- `computeMostImportantItem` (`downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) reads the sprint-view window once via `deps.getHerdrListHead(cwd, sprintWindow)`, then calls `scanOfferable(head.items, true, offerState)` to accumulate the single offer **and** the per-bucket nominees.
- The whole-backlog loop below it calls `scanOfferable(extendedItems, false, offerState)` — extension candidates feed only the single offer; the `withNominees:false` flag is the coded form of "the window is never widened to fill a bucket" (AC3 of WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P, documented at `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket").
- `scanOfferable` already implements the full sequential filter chain (classification → bucket skip → dispatched marker → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → code-freeze → in-flight guard → review-queue hold), with first-gate-wins rejection attribution.
- `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` (gates) grows geometrically (`max(current + DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX, current * 2)`), returns only items beyond `current`, and is fail-open; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` loops it to exhaustion under the same round cap and is used by `downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem` runs its own equivalent loop (`DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS`) and stops at the first single offer.
- `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` writes the v2 `offers` payload from `result.nominees`, falling back to a single-offer payload when `nominees` is empty; it logs `emptyOfferLogFields(result.attribution)` on the empty path.
- `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` iterates an entry's offers via `orderAdmissibleOffers` and already `continue`s to the next nominee when the audit budget refuses one.

## Desired change

When the visible list yields no nominee for a bucket, keep walking the SAME canonical ranking deeper into the project's backlog until each bucket has a nominee (or the backlog is exhausted). The visible window is a rendering bound, not a dispatch bound — the same principle already applied to the single-offer path. Concretely: run the extension whenever at least one bucket is unfilled (not only when the single offer is missing), pass the nominees flag through to the extended scan, stop as soon as all buckets are filled, and record which buckets were filled beyond the window plus how many extra items were read.

## Plan (plan skill, 13 Nov 2026)

**Decomposition decision: single leaf — no child items.** This is a Small/Medium `feature` whose ACs already enumerate the exact test cases (a)-(e), the docs edits and every touched file, and whose siblings of comparable size (`WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT`) shipped as single items. Splitting it would duplicate the AC list across children without isolating any independently deliverable slice, so planning stops at `plan_complete` and implementation continues on this item.

### Vertical slice, test-first

One vertical slice (code + tests + docs + observability), delivered in this order:

1. **Red tests first** — extend `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` with cases (a) and (b): a 20-item window whose buckets are all gated but whose tail holds an eligible `plan` and an eligible `implement` yields both nominees in canonical `COORDINATION_OFFER_BUCKETS` order; and a refused audit still leaves the entry's `prep` nominee dispatchable in the same tick. Cases (c), (d) and (e) are written in the same batch as regression guards (they must stay green before and after). Verify: changed-scope run via `/skill:test` fails on (a)/(b) and passes (c)/(d)/(e) pre-change.
2. **Signal plumbing (types)** — add an optional, additive field to the success variant of `MostImportantItemResult` (e.g. `filledBeyondWindow?: { buckets: CoordinationOfferKind[]; itemsRead: number }`), leaving every legacy union member untouched. Verify: build (typecheck) plus a check-in snapshot showing a window-sourced entry rendered byte-identically (field absent).
3. **Widening in `computeMostImportantItem`** — the whole-backlog loop runs while `offerState.singleOffer === null || nomineesByBucket.size < COORDINATION_OFFER_BUCKETS.length`, scans extended batches with `withNominees: true`, accumulates `itemsRead` per round **before** the early `break`, records the buckets first filled beyond the window, and stops as soon as every bucket is filled. `scanOfferable`'s own early stop stays the term-limit (single offer found AND all buckets filled). Verify: tests (a)-(e) green, plus the existing nominee/window and single-offer extension suites unchanged.
4. **Observability write** — `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` records the signal on the check-in entry and/or coordination decision-log entry (field or log fields naming buckets + items read); the `noCandidate` attribution path keeps reporting `windowSize = head.items.length + extendedTotal` exactly as today. Verify: a check-in test asserting the signal appears for a widened entry and is absent for a window-only entry.
5. **Docs and comment rewrite** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` "Per-bucket nominees from one head read" / "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" (line ~170) and the window statement at ~297 become "the visible window bounds rendering only; buckets are filled from the whole ranked backlog"; the AC3 commentary in `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` (`withNominees:false` doc) and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (~line 1134) is rewritten to match. Verify: grep for "never widened"/"Nothing is widened" returns only the new wording.
6. **Benchmark** — re-run `npm run benchmark:leader-tick-cost` on the owner side to confirm the tick stays within the existing ceiling with more reads per entry.

Between steps 3 and 4, re-read this description and the leader-side fall-through tests: any AC now covered differently is updated before the next step starts.

### Filters, cost, and fail-open (implementation invariants)

- **One read path:** bucket partitioning and the single offer both come from `getHerdrListHead`; the extension is a window widening of the same ordered stream, one `wl` spawn per round (never per bucket).
- **Filter chain unchanged:** the extended batches go through the identical `scanOfferable` sequence (classification → bucket skip → dispatched marker → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → code-freeze → in-flight guard → review-queue hold), first-gate-wins attribution included.
- **Bounded:** extension entered only when at least one bucket is unfilled; geometric growth; `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS` cap; walk stops when all buckets are filled.
- **Fail-open:** an absent/`{ok:false}`/throwing extension leaves the pre-change result (same tokens, same attribution, `nominees` unchanged) and never blocks dispatch.

### Decisions taken at plan time

- **`flagBudgetExhausted` side-effect amplification — accepted, documented in code.** Widening may now flag deeper attempt-exhausted items that were previously never visited. Gating the flag for extended candidates would make the filter chain conditional on scan depth, contradicting the "same filters, unchanged order" constraint; the flag is a producer-review marker, and the existing single-offer extension already exhibits exactly this behaviour. The implementation records this decision in a comment beside the flag call and in the docs paragraph.
- **Signal shape — union-additive.** An optional field rather than a new discriminant, so v1/v2 leaders and the check-in fallback keep byte-identical behaviour for window-only entries (see AC "Backwards compatibility").
- **`extendedTotal` accounting — unchanged on the empty path, corrected for the new signal.** `extendedTotal` is still only incremented for rounds that yield no offer, so `summariseEmptyOffer` window sizes do not shift; the new `itemsRead` counts every extended item read, including the round that filled the last bucket.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem`: the whole-backlog loop currently passes `withNominees:false` and only runs when the single offer is missing; the `scanOfferable` early-stop condition and the AC3 commentary need updating. `scanOfferable`, `emitNominees`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `MostImportantItemResult` / `CoordinationNominee`: carry the "filled beyond window" signal (bucket names + items read) without changing the legacy union members.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — write the signal onto the check-in entry and/or the coordination log entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` (`fetchWholeBacklogTail` is its exhaustion wrapper for the batch path; this change reuses `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` only — likely no change beyond doc comments).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `orderAdmissibleOffers` fall-through after a refused audit (regression coverage only).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — nominee/window tests, including the existing "never widened" assertion near AC3 (must be rewritten).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — "Per-bucket nominees from one head read" and "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" paragraphs; window-bounds-rendering statement.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher-post-fix-verification.md` — verification steps for a widened offer (if it enumerates offer evidence).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the ranked head beyond the window is stable between reads (same ranking function, same `wl` store); a concurrently changing backlog can yield a slightly different tail — acceptable, as it already is for the single-offer extension.
- **Risk — attribution drift:** deeper candidates now produce rejection entries; `summariseEmptyOffer` window sizes must keep reporting the window that was actually scanned (the existing `extendedTotal` already accumulates this) so operator diagnostics do not shift.
- **Risk — side-effect amplification:** `scanOfferable` flags attempt-budget-exhausted items (`flagBudgetExhausted`). Widening the scan can flag items that were previously never visited; this is the same side effect the existing extension already exhibits, but it becomes more likely — review that this is acceptable or gate it (document the decision in the implementation).
- **Risk — load:** each widened round is a `wl` list spawn on the owner instance's check-in path; bounded by geometric growth and the round cap, but visible on roots with thousands of items. The leader-tick benchmark should be re-run.
- **Risk — scope creep:** related opportunities (dispatched-marker TTL, in-flight invisibility, registered-root sweep) are recorded as separate items — do not absorb them here.
- **Assumption:** `prep` buckets (`plan`/`intake`/`risk-effort`) are as eligible for widening as `implement`/`audit`; the classifier order is unchanged.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P** (completed) — tier-aware offers. Its AC3 ("the window is never widened to fill a bucket") is **superseded** by this item; a comment has been recorded on that item.
- **WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT** (completed) — per-bucket nominees from one shared head read: the structure this item extends.
- **WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH** (completed) — made every work item a dispatch candidate; this item extends the same principle to the nominee buckets.
- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y / WL-0MW4ZOSD6004SAVD** — registered-root sweep (a *cross-root* mechanism, currently unconfigured on this machine); independent of this change.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (round-robin charge) and the audit-admission fix — the other two blockers in the 13 Nov dispatch starvation, on separate items.
- **WL-0MWC9J1OD001CT26 / WL-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG** — the two gated `tce-the-rising` plan items that motivated the evidence; out of scope here.

### Related work items (automated find-related report)

- **WL-0MWDVN2HN004CQ1O** — Leader iterates offers through unchanged filter chain with drain-aware tie-break (completed): the leader-side half this item relies on for fall-through.
- **WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT** — Per-bucket nominees computed from one shared head read (completed): the owner-side half being widened.
- **WL-0MWDVMVX50012RSU** — Coordination schema v2: bounded offers array with v1 migration-read (completed): the `offers` payload that will carry widened nominees unchanged.

### Related files (automated report)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Does intake need a producer interview for this item? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No. The item was created from a completed investigation with live evidence, a desired change, explicit ACs and a documented out-of-scope list; the remaining uncertainties are implementation-level and recorded as risks. Source: item description at intake time; repo inspection of `downtime-worker.coordination.ts`, `downtime-worker.gates.ts`, `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

That item deliberately excluded per-bucket widening (its AC3); this item supersedes exactly that constraint while keeping its one-read-per-bucket partitioning. Source: `wl show WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Per-bucket nominees from one head read".

- **Q:** Does the review-queue depth hold need to change so a deep implement can be offered? — **Answer (agent):** No. The hold stays an unchanged sequential filter; a deep implement nominee that the hold refuses must not become a nominee. Source: `scanOfferable` filter chain; `isImplementHeldByReviewGate`.

The ACs already enumerate the exact tests (a)-(e), the docs edits and every touched file, and comparably sized siblings (`WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT`) shipped as single items; decomposition would only duplicate the AC list.
